newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian police arrest 200 from Islamist group.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian police arrest 200 from Islamist group.

text.p: Egyptian police have arrested 200 suspected members of an Islamist group which believes in violence to change the government, set up an Islamic state and reform society, a government newspaper said on Saturday.
The group, known as the Qutbiyyin after late Moslem Brotherhood leader Sayyed Qutb, had close links with the Moslem Brotherhood, the newspaper al-Ahram reported.
Qutb, famous for his polemical work Signposts on the Path, died in prison in 1966 during the long persecution of the Brotherhood by president Gamal Abdel Nasser.
Al-Ahram said police made the arrests in nine provinces "some days ago" and investigations had shown that that the Moslem Brotherhood helped organise its provincial branches.
The group, in line with Sayyed Qutb's teachings, believes Egyptian society is in a state of pre-Islamic "ignorance" and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak is an infidel, it added.
Earlier this week Egyptian police arrested another group of 48 Islamists said to have connections with the Brotherhood.
Al-Ahram said the public prosecutor wanted to question a member of parliament from the opposition Labour Party, Ali Sayyed Fath al-Bab, in connection with this group.
The prosecutor may ask parliament to lift his immunity so that he can undergo interrogation, it added.
The Labour Party contains many members of the Brotherhood, which has been repeatedly denied legal recognition either as a political party or in any other form.

For many years the state largely tolerated the Brotherhood, a large and influential organisation, but for the past two years it has tried to equate it with the violent groups trying to overthrow the government by force. Brotherhood leaders say they oppose the use of violence for political ends.
